### Day 64: 2 Samuel 15:1–12
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-64-2-samuel-15-112.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 15:1-12
Points:
- Outward reunion does not equate to genuine spiritual reconciliation and emotional healing.
- Unresolved anger and bitterness consumed over a decade of Absalom's life.
- Absalom manipulated public grievances and played politics to enact revenge against his father.
- Harboring grudges traps a person in an internal prison that erodes character.
- Following Christ requires extending forgiveness even when offenders never acknowledge their wrongdoing.

### Absalom Makes a Play for the Throne
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/absalom-makes-play-for-throne
Passage: 2 Samuel 15:4
Points:
- Physical charisma and charm can easily mask an absence of godly character and devotion.
- Absalom used royal display and flattering promises of justice to steal people's allegiance.
- David's past sins and spiritual neglect blinded him to his son's brewing rebellion.
- Selfish ambition often masquerades as concern for the fairness and well-being of others.
- Believers and parents need spiritual discernment to perceive hidden motives and uncorrected misbehavior.
